He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]] and was selected in the first round of the [[2020 NBA draft]] by the [[Utah Jazz]]. ==Early life== Born in Lagos, Nigeria, Azubuike was the youngest of 5, with two older brothers and two older sisters.{{Cite news |url=https://nypost.com/2018/03/29/kansas-star-will-get-amazing-final-four-moment-seeing-mom/ |title=Kansas star will get amazing Final Four moment: Seeing Mom |last=Kussoy |first=Howard |date=March 29, 2018 |work=[[New York Post]] |archive-date=April 3, 2018 |access-date=April 3, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180403112538/https://nypost.com/2018/03/29/kansas-star-will-get-amazing-final-four-moment-seeing-mom/ |url-status=live }} His father, Fabian, was a police officer, and his mother, Florence, was a middle school teacher. Azubuike lost his father to an undiagnosed disease at the age of 10.{{Cite news |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2767373-think-reaching-the-final-4-is-tough-then-you-havent-met-kansas-udoka-azubuike |title=Think Reaching the Final 4 Is Tough? Then You Haven't Met Kansas' Udoka Azubuike |last=King |first=Jason |date=March 30, 2018 |work=Bleacher Report}} In 2012, he caught the attention of recruiters with [[Basketball Without Borders]] and was offered a scholarship to play basketball in the United States. ==High school career== Azubuike attended Potter's House Christian Academy in [[Jacksonville, Florida]]. His then assistant coach Harry Coxsome and his wife Donna took care of him and soon became his [[legal guardians]]. In his first high school game he was matched up against fellow future Kansas Jayhawk [[Joel Embiid]]. Azubuike was a four-year starter averaging 16.9 [[Points per game|points]] and 9.7 [[Rebounds per game|rebounds]] per game his senior year.{{Cite web |url=http://www.jacksonville.com/sports/high-schools/2016-01-28/story/potters-house-hoops-star-udoka-azubuike-commits-kansas |title=Potter's House hoops star Udoka Azubuike commits to Kansas On January 28, 2016, he announced his choice to play college basketball at the [[University of Kansas]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2016/01/28/udoka-azubuike-kansas-jayhawks-recruiting-commits |title=Four-star center Udoka Azubuike commits to Kansas |date=January 28, 2016 |access-date=March 10, 2018 |archive-date=March 10, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180310200629/https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2016/01/28/udoka-azubuike-kansas-jayhawks-recruiting-commits |url-status=live }} ==College career== ===Freshman year=== In his freshman season he started in six of the 11 games he played in before tearing [[ligament]]s in his left wrist, which ended his season.{{Cite web |url=http://www2.kusports.com/news/2016/dec/21/ku-freshman-udoka-azubuike-out-season-wrist-injury/ |title=KU freshman Udoka Azubuike out for the season with wrist injury |access-date=March 10, 2018 |archive-date=February 9, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180209134246/http://www2.kusports.com/news/2016/dec/21/ku-freshman-udoka-azubuike-out-season-wrist-injury/ |url-status=live }} Before the injury, he averaged 5.0 points, 4.4 rebounds, 1.6 [[Block (basketball)|blocks]], and 62.9% [[field goal percentage|field goal accuracy]]. ===Sophomore year=== For the [[2017–18 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|2017–18 season]], Kansas' coach [[Bill Self]] recruited [[Kansas Jayhawks football|Kansas football]] player James Sosinski to defend Azubuike during practice.{{Cite news |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article207362374.html |title='Pushing and shoving' Doke is this KU walk-on's job. He has bruises to prove it |last=Reiss |first=Aaron |date=March 29, 2018 |work=[[Kansas City Star]]}} Udoka started every game of the regular season but missed the [[2018 Big 12 men's basketball tournament|Big 12 Conference tournament]] after spraining his left [[medial collateral ligament|MCL]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article203968534.html |title=Udoka Azubuike out for Big 12 Tournament, KU hopeful he can return for NCAAs |last=Bedore the nation with a 77% field goal percentage for the season.{{Cite web |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/udoka-azubuike-1.html |title=Udoka Azubuike |website=Sports-Reference.com |access-date=April 3, 2018 |archive-date=March 20, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220320201946/https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/udoka-azubuike-1.html |url-status=live }} His field goal percentage broke the single-season record for Kansas and the [[Big 12 Conference]].{{Cite news |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article207122189.html |title=A former KU center analyzes the game of Jayhawks big man Udoka Azubuike |last=Bedore |first=Gary |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180709153554/https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article207122189.html |url-status=live }} This high percentage was in part due to the majority of his field goals being [[slam dunks]], which typically have a higher completion percentage than jump shots or layups. He had more dunks than any other college player going back to the 2009–2010 season.{{Cite news |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article209693674.html |title=This decade, no player has done what KU's Udoka Azubuike just did |last=Newell |first=Jesse |date=April 24, 2018 |work=Kansas City Star |access-date=April 24, 2018 |archive-date=April 25, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180425030737/http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article209693674.html |url-status=live }} He was awarded All-Big 12 third team by the conference's coaches{{Cite web |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/article203429049.html |title=Devonté Graham, Bill Self take home coaches' All-Big 12 basketball awards |last=Newell |first=Jesse |date=March 4, 2018 |website=Kansas City Star |access-date=April 5, 2018}} and second team by the [[Associated Press|AP]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/article203722914.html |title=Devonté Graham, Bill Self win AP All-Big 12 awards |last=Newell |first=Jesse |date=March 6, 2018 |website=Kansas City Star |access-date=April 5, 2018 |archive-date=April 6, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180406101910/http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/article203722914.html |url-status=live }} On April 20, 2018, Azubuike announced his intention to enter the [[2018 NBA draft]]. He did not initially hire an agent, which would allow him to return before the combine.{{cite web |last=Medcalf |first=Myron |date=April 20, 2018 |title=Kansas' Udoka Azubuike entering draft without agent |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/23261307 |access-date=November 28, 2023 |website=ESPN.com |archive-date=August 13, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230813200428/https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/23261307 |url-status=live }} Azubuike was one of a record-high 69 prospects invited to the [[NBA Draft Combine]] that year. On May 17, he measured out to be a near-7-foot-tall center (with shoes on) weighing in at {{convert|274|lb}} and holding the second-longest wingspan at {{convert|7|ft|7|in}}, behind only [[Mohamed Bamba]].{{cite web | url=http://stats.nba.com/draft/combine-anthro/#!?sort=WINGSPAN&dir=1 | title=Draft Combine Anthrometric | access-date=May 17, 2018 | archive-date=May 17, 2018 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180517215232/http://stats.nba.com/draft/combine-anthro/#!?sort=WINGSPAN&dir=1 | url-status=live }} On May 30, 2018, he announced his intent to withdraw from the draft and return to Kansas for his junior season.{{cite web |last=Newell |first=Jesse |date=May 30, 2018 |title=Udoka Azubuike withdraws from NBA Draft. Here's what his return means for KU |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article212176139.html |access-date=November 28, 2023 |website=KansasCity.com (2020–2023)=== Azubuike was selected with the 27th pick in the first round of the [[2020 NBA draft]] by the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite news|first=Eric|last=Walden|title=Utah Jazz take Kansas center Udoka Azubuike at No. 27, trade center Tony Bradley and 38th pick to Pistons|url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/jazz/2020/11/18/utah-jazz-pick-kansas/|work=[[Salt Lake Tribune]]|date=November 18, 2020|access-date=November 18, 2020}} On November 24, 2020, the Jazz announced that they had signed Azubuike.{{cite web|first=JP|last=Chunga|title=Jazz sign Azubuike and Hughes|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-sign-azubuike-and-hughes|date=November 24, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=November 24, 2020|archive-date=February 7, affiliate, the [[Salt Lake City Stars]], for the start of the 2021 G League season, making his G League debut on February 10, 2021. He made his NBA playoff debut on June 14 in game 4 of the 2021 Western Conference Semifinals, recording a rebound in a minute and nine seconds of action in a 118–104 loss to the [[2020–21 Los Angeles Clippers season|Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web | url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202106140LAC.html | title=2021 NBA Western Conference Semifinals Game 4: Jazz vs Clippers, June 14, 2021 | access-date=August 29, 2023 | archive-date=August 29, 2023 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230829023527/https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202106140LAC.html | url-status=live }} On March 25, 2022, Azubuike underwent right foot surgery and was ruled out for the rest of the 2021–22 season.{{cite web|first=Angie|last=Treasure|title=Udoka Azubuike Injury Update|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/udoka-azubuike-injury-update|website=NBA.com|date=March 25, 2022|access-date=March 25, 2022}} ===Phoenix Suns (2023–2024)=== On August 8, 2023, Azubuike signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web|first=Dana|last=Gauruder|title=Suns Sign Udoka Azubuike To Two-Way Deal|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/08/suns-agree-to-two-way-deal-with-udoka-azubuike.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=August 8, 2023|access-date=August 8, 2023|archive-date=August 9, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230809220622/https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/08/suns-agree-to-two-way-deal-with-udoka-azubuike.html|url-status=live}}{{cite web|title=Suns Sign Udoka Azubuike|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-sign-udoka-azubuike|website=NBA.com|access-date=November 28, 2023|archive-date=October 21, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231021053018/https://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-sign-udoka-azubuike|url-status=live}} He made his team debut on October 28 by putting up 2 points and 3 rebounds during 6 minutes of action in a 126–104 win over his former team, the [[Utah Jazz]]. On December 20, Azubuike recorded his first double-double with the Suns with 11 points and a season-high 11 rebounds in a 120–105 loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]]. ===Budućnost VOLI (2024–2025)=== On August 19, 2024, Azubuike signed with [[KK Budućnost|Budućnost VOLI]] of the [[Prva A Liga]].{{cite web|title=Rim protektor: Judoka novi centar
